questions.question: What is a unimodal distribution?
options: A distribution with more than one mean
A distribution with variance zero only

questions.question: What is a multimodal distribution?
options: A distribution with exactly one mode
A distribution with no random variable
A distribution with only one outcome
A distribution with more than one mode

questions.question: What does a unimodal distribution look like conceptually?
options: It must be symmetric about zero

questions.question: What can several peaks in a multimodal distribution suggest?
options: That the variable is not random

questions.question: What kind of model can create multimodal distributions?
Is a normal distribution unimodal or multimodal?
A distribution has exactly two modes. What is it called?
A mixture of weekday and weekend demand distributions may be what?
Exam scores from two very different preparation groups can form what?
If a PMF has one unique largest mass, how would the distribution usually be classified by modes?
How is multimodality related to mode?
options: It is defined by having a large variance only
It means the mean is negative
It is defined by having more than one mode

questions.question: Why can mixtures create multimodal distributions?
options: Mixtures force every component to have the same center
Different components can contribute distinct peaks

questions.question: Why does 'multimodal' not simply mean 'high variance'?
options: It is exactly the same as variance
It only applies to deterministic variables
It concerns the number of peaks, not just spread
It means the distribution has no modes

questions.question: A density has peaks near $-3$, $0$, and $4$. How is it classified?
A bell-shaped density with one peak is usually classified as what?
Suppose two customer segments have well-separated purchase amounts. What might their combined distribution show?
Can a distribution be multimodal even if each component of a mixture is unimodal?
options: Yes, separated unimodal components can combine into several peaks
No, mixtures preserve one mode exactly, regardless of the specific input chosen.
Only if the distribution is discrete

questions.question: Seeing two clear peaks in an empirical distribution most directly suggests which modelling concern?
options: The distribution must be normal, no matter which values are selected.
The data may mix two subgroups or mechanisms.

questions.question: A student calls a two-peaked distribution unimodal because it has one mean. What is wrong?
options: A distribution cannot have a mean and modes.
Two peaks imply no random variable
Unimodality depends on modes, not on the number of means
